description: Registered fault/crash hooks in LiteDB/ and the evidence that claims each one. Maintained by .github/scripts/check_fault_points.py; see docs/rules/safety-evidence.md.

models.exception: An API or I/O operation fails and unwinding/cleanup runs.
models.process-death: The process or owner dies without graceful disposal; OS cache and surviving processes remain.
models.modeled-power-loss: A fault-model stream/device keeps only durable bytes (lost, torn or reordered unsynced writes).
models.device: An actual OS/VM reset or physical-device campaign.
models.corrupt-input: Damaged or unsupported persisted input must be detected without silent acceptance.
models.interleaving: The hook pauses or orders work to force a concurrent interleaving; not a failure by itself.
models.capability: The hook simulates a platform capability (for example unsupported sync), not a failure.

hooks.name: wal-rebase-before-anchor-flush

evidence.proves: Actual stream flush/rewrite failures at this boundary publish terminal stop before queued confirmation, preserve WAL bytes on later attempts, and recover the seeded document twice from saved files.

hooks.gap: Exception and forced writer interleaving evidence; this new marker has no process-death or modeled-power-loss campaign claim.

injectors.name: OwnershipStage
injectors.protocol: Shared terminal completion, core-close and snapshot-open boundaries

evidence.proves: The mapped holder pauses before its facade lifetime lock; a successor reserves its actual local lease and waits at native main before dead-owner cleanup resumes, without the old cleanup erasing the new lease.
Commit/rollback/core-close/Dispose cuts release local and native ownership for both ordinary and pinned holders, followed by immediate peer admission and two cold indexed payload checks.
An injected read-only snapshot open failure follows the normal writable fallback after real mutex abandonment and a conflicting WRITE byte.

injectors.name: WriteRetry
injectors.protocol: Native WRITE conflict with a held main mutex

evidence.proves: A real abandoned thread leaves live handles in its surviving process; a controlled byte release permits acquisition, persistent conflict times out without stealing ownership and a later retry succeeds.

Plain/encrypted mapped owners hit three failed registrations then retry, commit and admit 20 writes from a separate process while the owner stays alive; cold indexed payload and sentinel oracles exclude aborted rows.

injectors.name: PublicationStage
injectors.protocol: ABI-2 mapped writer publication and recovery fences

evidence.proves: Real SharedEngine construction/close hits production reuse stores with asserted reuse and marker reachability, two child deaths per cut and two indexed payload/sentinel recovery checks.
A process killed at each mapped writer publication fence is recoverable; acknowledged payloads and indexes remain complete and the next writer can repeat recovery.
Retained DMS and an actual accepted snapshot survive two successor deaths at each internal writer/open/structural cut; exact generations, payloads and indexes survive protected recovery twice.
Two separately captured group barriers with a pending later append publish only the prefix covered by the completed barrier.
Stopped cores cannot publish commits, clear recovery fencing or retain native WRITE after any tested grouped barrier failure.
Each injected partial acquisition releases WRITE and local ownership before an independently threaded protected recovery succeeds.
A genuinely warm streamed snapshot survives writer death at each writer/open/commit fence and repeated recovery with exact indexed payloads.
Every reached publication stage samples at most a sync-covered prefix; failed sync remains fenced and cannot reenable warm status.

injectors.gap: Linux x64 only; no device reset or ARM memory-ordering claim.

injectors.name: AdmissionStage

evidence.proves: Each mapped sequence/authority/field/recheck cut rejects a crossed publication and samples complete 64-bit epochs.
Crossing any load in either status sample rejects even a same-version publication; no query executes warm and no record leaks.
Every status cut and the post-record cut throws before execution, releases any new generation, and leaves the next read usable.

injectors.gap: Bounded Linux x64 SC/CLR evidence; no ARM or device memory-ordering qualification.

injectors.name: RequestStage
injectors.protocol: ABI-2 expiring FIFO writer requests before native acquisition

evidence.proves: Both request cuts throw, clear their record and permit the next protected writer with cold indexed data preserved.
A child killed or SIGSTOPped at publication cannot prevent the next requester acquiring main after the holder commits.
A queued local request cannot lend its priority; twelve real handoffs use fresh tickets behind a remote request.
A real remote renewal after the sampled clock preserves priority until native admission and both callers make progress.

injectors.gap: Linux x64 only; no Windows/macOS or device reset qualification.

injectors.name: SimulateWaitError
injectors.protocol: Mapped Shared native futex result handling

evidence.proves: EINTR and repeated shared wakes preserve the retained holder; actual 20/1 ms arguments follow pressure.
A forced unexpected native wait errno drains the real active operation before releasing main and WRITE; cold indexed data survives.

observers.HandoffPublication: Carries the existing thread-local PublicationStage injector from an operation to its retained holder teardown; no additional publication boundary.
observers.AtCrashPoint: Per-engine delivery of the process-crash family's named points (CrashPoint also calls SimulateProcessCrash); each name is registered under hooks with its own evidence, so this delegate adds no boundary of its own.
observers.BeforeCreatePipe: Interleaving hook before the coordinator creates its pipe; no persistent state changes at this point.
observers.BeforePageRead: Observes page reads (position, origin) to force read interleavings; faults use SimulateDiskReadFail.
observers.BeforeReadLength: Interleaving hook before a file length is read; no persistent state changes.
observers.BeforeWaitOutHeartbeats: Interleaving hook in coordinator status-page heartbeats; in-memory coordination only.
observers.CoreStage: Ownership observer: reports the opened/closing/closed lifecycle of each Shared core that requires writer exclusion; it never injects a fault.
observers.CoordinationStage: Observes in-process Shared admission stages (opening, lease-published, admitted, expiring); lease-file persistence is listed under unhookedTransitions.
observers.FinalizedInUse: Detects page buffers finalized while in use (leak diagnostics), not a fault boundary.
observers.HandshakeStage: Observes coordinator handshake stages to force interleavings; no persistent state changes.
observers.LevelRandomFactory: Makes vector index level selection deterministic for tests; not a fault boundary.
observers.ObserveCacheEviction: Measurement hook proving cache eviction happened; not a fault boundary.
observers.Observer: Reachability observer: runs on the thread that hit a marker (for example a fault-point site) so a fuzz oracle can evaluate an invariant there; it never injects a fault.
observers.ObserveSortSpill: Measurement hook proving a sort spilled to disk; not a fault boundary.
observers.Releasing: Ownership observer: runs just before a Shared connection releases its native writer mutex so an oracle can check every protected core finished teardown; it never injects a fault.
observers.SnapshotCaptured: Interleaving hook after checkpoint captures its snapshot; checkpoint persistence is covered by checkpoint-stage and process-crash hooks.
observers.BeforeFinalClose: Pauses the last Direct facade close before engine disposal; DirectProcessHost_Tests.Open_during_last_close_waits_then_opens_fresh forces the open/close interleaving.
observers.UnsupportedVolume: Overrides native volume qualification for fail-closed admission capability testing; no fallback is enabled.
observers.WaitObserved: Observes the mapped holder sample, pressure recheck, native wait and return to force wake interleavings and inspect the actual timeout/error; no persistent mutation.

unhookedTransitions.transition: Directory-entry persistence of the recovery marker and the backup/install renames: rebuild-install hooks fault the operations, but the model does not lose unsynced directory entries.
Reader lease-file publication, renewal and expiry have observer stages only (CoordinationStage); no registered fault point interrupts them.
